reason: Refuted as proposed; the procedural core is sound but the text misreads the evidence. (1) The premise that d1 = K2 - #35 reads lowrefine alone is false in the slow world. K2 carries the 8.0 h insertion gate (DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=28800), and its forecast is F = 7.87 h (scan_plancheck 22:30Z). That leaves a 0.13 h margin, smaller than the 818-1179 s start-up jitter between identical kernels. Clips run alphabetically with public and private mixed, so late public clips can silently lose the insertion (worth ~+0.001 on public). #35 ran under x138's 7.5 h repair deadline with L35 in (6.72, 7.73] h, so it may itself be degraded. (2) Magnitude: the lowrefine ceiling is |d| <= ~2.4e-4 (+29 edges, +33 nodes, +1 fork on the dummies; RT2 value notes). A displayed d1 <= -0.002 needs a real drop > 0.001 (#35 in [0.9535, 0.9545), K2 < 0.9525). That is 4x or more past the ceiling, so the trigger world is mostly insertion-gate timing or a hidden-data bug, not a lowrefine sign. In that world K1 (exp58t) has the SAME 28,800 s insertion gate and repairs nothing. Meanwhile the rule would evict the twin (no insertion, no gate, the file least exposed to timing) from F2 in favour of exp52 (0.950). (3) 'd2 alone never drops lowrefine' inverts the evidence. d2 = twin - #34 is the cleaner read: no insertion, no gate, #34 L <= 6.46 h, twin repair 219 s vs K2 509 s. (4) Duplicate: the same round's scan_plancheck PC3-01/02 proposes the same pre-registration, but with a timing-confound clause and with d2 also able to close lowrefine; round 1 RT2's salvage already said to pre-commit before the scores. Feasibility itself is fine: it is 22:47Z 25 Sep and neither K2 nor the twin is submitted yet (scores ~06:30-08:00Z). It is text only, so byte-identical and fail-soft do not apply, and it costs at most one conditional 26 Sep slot, with K1 already dummy-gated (sha == exp57b dummy). The [OK] items (K1 submit, twin floor 0.952) correctly stay with the user.
fix: Write ONE LOWREFINE READ block into CONTEXT before 06:00Z 26 Sep, time-stamped before any K2/twin score in poll.log, merging PC3-01/02 with these corrections. (a) Primary lowrefine read = d2 = twin - #34: d2 <= -0.002 closes lowrefine under R3. (b) d1 = K2 - #35 counts as a lowrefine read ONLY if L(K2) <= 8.0 h is proven, i.e. COMPLETE seen by the poller before 08:01Z 26 Sep. If L(K2) > 8.0 h or it is unproven, a d1 <= -0.002 is a TIMING CONFOUND (branch-C logic): lowrefine is kept, the twin stays F2 by f2, F1 = K2 unless K1 scores >= K2 + 0.002 (R7), and the D4/deadline-move trigger of v4 item 5 is raised for the user. (c) Proven L(K2) <= 8.0 h AND d1 <= -0.002 AND d2 <= -0.001: lowrefine closed; K1 (exp58t v1) submitted in the next 26 Sep slot [needs OK]; F1 = K1 once scored, R5-admissible and >= 0.953; F2 = exp52 (never exp58nt, a byte-copy of x138). (d) Any d1/d2 disagreement beyond (c) keeps lowrefine: they share the embryo and the lowrefine nodes, so disagreement points to a confound, not a sign. (e) Twin floor 0.952 [OK] only when lowrefine is kept, otherwise 0.953 per f2. Record F = 7.87 h next to it, and keep the poller alive 07:00-08:30Z (do not restart it then).
realistic_gain: Procedural only. Expected private gain ~+1e-5 to +5e-5: the triggers are rare (P(d1 <= -0.002) ~0.03-0.05; P(twin 0.952) ~0.05-0.1) and lowrefine's true effect is <= ~2.4e-4. The main value is avoiding a result-dependent finals choice, plus rank insurance in the rare lowrefine-bug world. As proposed (no timing clause, d2 ignored) the expected gain is ~0 or slightly negative: in the timing world it would swap F2 from the twin to exp52 and spend a slot on K1, which has the same insertion gate. Cost: 0 GPU, 0 code, at most 1 conditional slot on 26 Sep.
